doc: Browser timing as explicit, cancellable mechanism (LCP-010): the engine asks for a wake-up and is told, exactly once, whether it fired or was cancelled. Debounce, throttle, polling and retry are engine policy built from these; the pack holds no policy. Interval and prioritized task scheduling are deliberately absent: no reference case or measurement yet justifies them (docs/34).

variants.name: timeout
variants.doc: Wake after at least delayMs milliseconds (0 to 2147483647).

variants.name: animationFrame
variants.doc: Wake before the browser's next repaint.

variants.name: idle
variants.doc: Wake when the browser is idle, or after timeoutMs if given. Unsupported where the browser has no idle callback.

types.name: ScheduleResult
types.doc: Exactly one per request. A cancelled request never also fires.

variants.name: Fired
variants.doc: The wake-up happened; elapsedMs is the measured time since the request was accepted.

variants.name: IdleFired
variants.doc: An idle wake-up: whether it came from the timeout, and the idle time the browser estimated was left.

variants.name: InvalidDelay
variants.doc: delayMs or timeoutMs outside 0..2147483647; nothing was scheduled.

variants.name: Unsupported
variants.doc: This browser does not implement the primitive; nothing was scheduled.

variants.name: Cancelled
variants.doc: The engine cancelled the request before it fired.
